title: Token-aligned kernel dispatch and KV resiliency with continuous-batch fusion for Llama/Mistral/Qwen
author: Aisha Moreno
description: Motivation: Production workloads showed recurring tail-latency and KV eviction storms when serving mixed-model traffic (Llama/Mistral/Qwen) with heterogeneous token lengths and mixed GQA/MQA layouts. This PR introduces a set of coordinated runtime changes: 1) Token-aligned kernel dispatcher that groups requests by token-shift boundaries to avoid partial-head misalignment and reduce kernel polymorphism penalties. 2) KV resiliency layer that adds a soft-snapshot and watermark-driven eviction path so transient memory pressure no longer triggers full cache churn across slabs. 3) Continuous-batch fusion (lane-aware fusion) that coalesces many small requests into fused microbatches while keeping per-request latency SLOs via prioritized draining and lane affinity. 4) Per-model microkernel hints for known quirks (LLama head packing, Mistral attention stride, Qwen block-size alignment) so the scheduler can pick optimized kernel paths without expensive runtime probes. Implementation summary: token-aligned-dispatch introduces a light-weight fingerprint for the first 8 tokens and a shift-canonicalization step before kernel selection; the dispatcher prefers already-warmed kernel variants for identical shift classes. The KV resiliency component adds epoched snapshotting, an eviction watermark that triggers background compaction, and a degraded-read fallback that serves KV-miss slices from prefix-cache while compaction finishes. Continuous-batch fusion implements a lane allocator with soft-timers and a priority queue that favors latency-sensitive routes; fusion is abortable on headroom pressure. Performance: microbench on Llama-13B (open-proxy trace) showed 14% median latency improvement and 22% 95th-percentile reduction; combined workloads with MQA/GQA saw up to 1.35x throughput on saturated GPU pools with nearly identical quality. Safety and compatibility: changes are opt-in via runtime flags at deploy time and default to disabled for private deployments; added a compatibility matrix to models/quirks mapping. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for dispatcher and KV snapshotting - [x] Perf harness for fusion scenarios - [x] Back-compat layer for existing KVCaches - [x] Documentation in runtime/ops and models/quirks - [x] Manual canary rollout and observability dashboards Updated Linear tasks ENG-5124 and ENG-5179 with rollout notes and post-canary metrics.

review_comments: Jonah Kim: Nice direction. Two asks: (1) can we make the token fingerprint length configurable via a flag? (2) please add a short doc about how per-model hints are validated during model onboarding.
Author (Aisha): Answered in PR thread: fingerprint length is a runtime flag with safe defaults and we added a validation hook during model onboarding that rejects hints with unsupported opcodes.
Priya Desai: Observability: we need additional k/v metrics for snapshot latency and compaction time. The current dashboards don't expose compaction stalls.
Author (Aisha): Added metrics kv.snapshot.duration_ms and kv.compaction.backlog_count and wired them into the canary dashboard. See docs link in the artifacts section.
Marco Alvarez: In perf runs, Qwen head alignment improves throughput but caused a rare kernel fallback in mixed-precision mode on Ampere nodes. Can we gate that path behind a hw-cap check?
Author (Aisha): Added a hardware capability probe that disables the alignment-based kernel on unsupported cards; fallback path remains the same.
Jonah Kim: Approving after CI rerun and metrics added. Verified canary metrics look good for the sample tenant.
